source.title: Data-driven Circuit Discovery for Interpretability of Language Models
source.authors: Daking Rai; M. Geva; Zi-Yu Yao

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether IOI circuits generalize across prompt variants and finds that transfer is often incomplete or asymmetric, refining the claim that one circuit carries the behavior across variants.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI circuit faithfulness across prompt variants and models, transfer summaries, and method-related results. It does not test the original 26-head circuit or assign its stated head roles. Results about DCD clustering are not separately cataloged here; the clearest directly relevant IOI transfer results and reported method limitation are retained.
record.test_reason: The study finds EAP-IG edge circuits (top 5% of edges) for IOI variants in GPT-2 Small, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It tests whether each variant's circuit stays faithful on other variants: name order, voice, 3-person, filler and letter labels. Results bear on V6 (one mechanism across prompt formats) and on the prompt-distribution part of V5. These are automatically discovered edge circuits, not the original 26-head circuit, and no head roles are assigned.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors show that a faithful circuit can merge distinct mechanisms, and that variants of one task (including IOI names vs letter labels) can rely on different mechanisms. They propose grouping examples before discovery (DCD), treating the resulting clusters as hypotheses rather than definitive mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses automated edge-attribution circuit discovery (primarily EAP-IG, with EAP and E-ACT checks) and evaluates faithfulness across variants. It does not reproduce the original head-by-head circuit analysis or its head-role patching experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI circuit transfer varies with prompt variant and model. The paper also reports substantially weak EAP IOI circuits on GPT-2 at the 0.05 edge budget; EAP-IG and E-ACT are used as method checks. Alternative faithfulness metrics are not tested.

fits_no_version.finding: A single circuit discovered on a 50/50 IOI–sequence-completion mixture is faithful to both tasks (e.g. GPT-2 0.63/0.63), while each pure circuit fails on the other task. Most of the mixed circuit's edges come from the two task-specific circuits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High faithfulness of an IOI circuit does not establish that it reflects a single mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: At a 5% edge budget, EAP circuits for GPT-2 IOI explain their own data poorly (6 of 7 in-distribution values below 0.3, minimum −0.85), while EAP-IG and E-ACT circuits do well.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether automated discovery finds a faithful IOI circuit at a fixed budget depends on the attribution method.

record.problems: The study does not directly test the original 26-head circuit or its stated roles. Variant-transfer tests use 200-prompt test sets and a bootstrap-based threshold; some GPT-2 IOI EAP circuits explain their in-distribution data poorly at the reported budget. The authors also note that faithfulness alone can combine distinct mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix contains detailed cross-variant faithfulness matrices and figures across additional IOI variant pairs, methods and circuit sizes. They were not all extracted individually; the aggregate IOI transfer outcomes, all IOI pairs explicitly reported as failing in both directions, and the explicit EAP limitation were retained. DCD clustering composition and best-of-K faithfulness results were omitted because they do not directly test the original IOI head classes or roles.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, their 7 classes and roles, and the faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria are not examined.
No name-mover ablation and no self-repair or backup-head test.
IOI circuits are found in Llama and Qwen, but no head classes or roles are identified or compared, and there are no checkpoints.
No comparison of EAP, EAP-IG or E-ACT circuits with the original circuit, and no alternative ablation types or metrics.
Ablation type and metric choices are not varied; only prompt distribution is tested, and only for edge circuits rather than the original.
The original circuit is not evaluated on the variants; only variant-specific edge circuits are.

missing.what: E-ACT (direct edge ablation) cross-variant results for GPT-2 IOI. 2-person circuit on letter: 0.62 vs 0.90 in-distribution. Letter circuit on 2-person: 0.65 vs 0.94. 2-person circuit on 3-person: 0.77 vs 1.06. This shows the names/letter failure is not specific to EAP-IG.
Per-pair IOI syntax results (ABBA vs BABA vs passive). On Llama these circuits transfer closely (values about 0.85–1.02), the main evidence that name order does not change the circuit.
Variant-specific Jaccard overlap for IOI: domain axis 0.30–0.39, versus 0.58 between disjoint halves of the same variant.
DCD-Cluster groups IOI name and letter prompts into separate clusters on all three models, with cluster circuits covering different variants.

record.verdict_notes: Records r5 and r7 have the transfer directions reversed, and the noise floors in r4–r7 are shifted by one row against Table 14. All shortfalls still exceed the corrected floors, so the both-way failures stand. For r1–r7, the state field is assessed against V6; read against V5 the same rows are observed. A supports label for V6 was not given because the pairs that transfer both ways are not identified in any row. GPT-2 has low accuracy on 3-person and filler prompts, which weakens mechanism readings for those GPT-2 pairs.

versions.untested_parts: The paper discovers edge circuits for IOI but does not test the original 26 attention heads, their seven classes or stated roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
No ablation of main name-mover heads or test of self-repair is reported.
The study compares circuits across models and tasks but does not test whether the original head classes and roles recur or are reused for other tasks.

The paper uses EAP-IG, EAP and E-ACT in its experiments, but does not establish whether these methods recover essentially the same circuit as the original method; it does not compare alternative evaluation metrics.
It tests sensitivity to IOI prompt variants and circuit-discovery methods, but not alternative faithfulness metrics. It does not directly evaluate the original 26-head circuit.

It tests IOI variants including name order, letter labels, passive syntax, filler text and three-person prompts, but does not test the original 26-head circuit across them or establish coverage of arbitrary templates and prompts.

relation.reason: The study directly measures IOI circuit faithfulness across prompt variants, bearing on V5 and V6.

tranche.reason: Cross-variant transfer failures provide results that the broad same-mechanism claim needs qualification, and support prompt-dependent faithfulness.

source_check.notes: Row states are interpreted for V6; the corresponding V5 state is observed. GPT-2 accuracy is only 60.8% on three-person and 68.4% on filler prompts, so some aggregate transfer losses may reflect task difficulty; the original 26-head circuit is not directly evaluated.

statements.problem: The counts and asymmetry are correct, but a blanket limits_scope label combines successful, asymmetric and bidirectionally failed transfer conditions.

statements.correction: Three-person variants: evaluated using newly discovered edge circuits. Original fixed 26-head circuit: not directly evaluated; inferred from the experimental design.
